title: Walk Slowly, but Never Backward
coreMove: When stuck preparing, convert the next hour into reps performed rather than time logged.

exampleSpecs.domain: a community college ceramics student deciding whether to throw fifty rough pots this month or perfect one
exampleSpecs.audience: a learner who confuses studying a craft with practicing it
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether her end-of-semester portfolio shows real skill growth or one polished beginner piece
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she catches herself preparing — sketching glazes, rereading the textbook — and reframes the question as how many times her hands touch clay this week

exampleSpecs.domain: a junior associate at an immigration law firm who keeps re-outlining a brief instead of writing a draft
exampleSpecs.audience: a knowledge worker mistaking research for progress
exampleSpecs.stakes: a filing deadline three days out and a partner who will read whatever exists at 9am Friday
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the scene lands on the moment she opens a blank document and writes one bad paragraph, registering that the bad paragraph is the habit forming

exampleSpecs.domain: two friends planning a half-marathon training block over text messages
exampleSpecs.audience: a beginner runner who has bought gear three times without ever finishing a week
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether September's race is real or another aborted plan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: one friend pushes back on the elaborate training spreadsheet and proposes thirty short runs in thirty days, even ones under a mile, with the explicit logic that frequency builds the runner

exampleSpecs.domain: a high school band director rebuilding the brass section after a year of cancelled rehearsals
exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher choosing between long perfect rehearsals and short frequent ones
exampleSpecs.stakes: a winter concert eight weeks away and students who have lost the embouchure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the shift from one ninety-minute weekly rehearsal to four twenty-minute daily ones, with the specific observation that the students stopped dreading the horn case

exampleSpecs.domain: a dispatcher at a regional ambulance service journaling about her abandoned watercolor practice
exampleSpecs.audience: a hobbyist who treats the absence of a perfect setup as permission to skip
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether the painting habit survives a third move in two years
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she names the precise lie — that she needs the right desk, the right light — and decides that ten minutes on the kitchen counter counts as a rep

exampleSpecs.domain: a hospital pharmacist reviewing a six-month attempt to learn conversational Tagalog
exampleSpecs.audience: an adult learner whose progress has stalled
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether she can hold a basic conversation with her father-in-law at his birthday in July
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she audits her log and sees that the eleven days of perfect hour-long sessions taught her less than the forty days of five-minute flashcard reps would have
